distractors.reason: We don't say 'look at my little sister' to mean take care of her. 'Look at' means to direct your eyes toward something.
'Look for' means to search for something. We don't say 'look for my little sister' to mean take care of her.
'Look to' means to rely on someone for help, not to take care of them. We say 'look after', not 'look to'.

example_sentence: Can you look ___ my little sister this afternoon?
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często wybierają 'look at' lub 'look for', ponieważ nie łączą od razu przyimka 'after' z znaczeniem opieki. Poprawnie: 'look after my little sister'.
explanation: In English, 'look after' means to take care of a person or thing. Here 'after' does not refer to time; it expresses responsibility for someone.

related_collocations.example: I am looking for my keys.
I wait for my dad after school.

memory_tip: LOOK AFTER = take care of someone | LOOK AT = see with your eyes | LOOK FOR = search for something
